scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: SH-CS (Customer Service Director, requester) asked for a single AI agent that auto-answers dispute tickets and autonomously "fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills" (CL-01).
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from 610/590 (Jun/Jul 2026) to 1180/1260 (Aug/Sep 2026) (E-07).
Majority of disputed bills carry ACTUAL read type (1785) rather than ESTIMATED (1240) (E-02).
Manual-read route completion is 0.88 against a 0.95 target across 9200 accounts, Aug-Sep 2026 (E-05).
Dispute ticket response times are within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d SLA) (E-03), so slow response handling is not the driver.
No tariff rate changes are logged in the observed period (E-01).
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1220/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-07) because a change to billing import validation rules around August is causing bills to be issued incorrectly even on accounts with actual (non-estimated) meter reads, as shown by disputed bills skewing to ACTUAL read type (1785) over ESTIMATED (1240) (E-02). This rules out AMI-read delivery failure and field-manual-read handoff failure as the dominant mechanism (both contradicted by E-02), and rules out tariff change (E-01) and slow ticket response handling (E-03) as drivers.

challenges.rationale: ER-1: premise E-02 revised by E-12: re-read under E-12 (accepted premise check) — PR-ROOT: E-12 confirms a specific import-rejection mechanism only for the 1240 ESTIMATED-type disputed bills (all AMI-channel), giving no evidence the rule change also produces incorrect bills on the 1785 ACTUAL-type bills that the root problem relies on as its key differentiator.; PR-CHAIN-3: The confirmed rejection mechanism in E-12 explains only the ESTIMATED-type subset of disputes (reads rejected then substituted as estimates); it provides no evidence the same mechanism produces incorrect bills on ACTUAL-read accounts, which is this premise's explicit claim and the majority of disputes.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-TICKET-RESPONSE-FRAMING.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a customer-service response/handling problem (slow or inadequate ticket answers), not a billing-accuracy problem, so an auto-answering agent would resolve it.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules (e.g. estimate-substitution logic) around August is causing more bills to be issued incorrectly.

H-AMI-READ-DEGRADATION.statement: AMI register reads from the vendor (Telemetrix) are failing to deliver or validate correctly in the nightly export, forcing more estimate substitutions and wrong AMI-based bills.

H-FIELD-READ-HANDOFF-FAILURE.statement: Manual meter reads from the contracted field service are failing to deliver or are semantically invalid in the daily upload, causing estimate substitution and billing errors concentrated in manually-read accounts.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTFALL.statement: MeterWorks field staffing/route capacity has dropped since August, causing missed manual reads, more estimated bills, and the dispute surge.

H-IMPORT-REJECTS-HIGH-CONSUMPT.statement: The billing import validation rule rejects AMI reads flagged as high-consumption (billing_import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution even though a valid AMI read was received before cutoff, accounting for 1184 of 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills.

H-BV17-SCOPE-ACTUAL-READS.statement: BV-17's high-consumption check compares raw register value to 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling applied, and its scope is not stated as AMI-only, so it may also trigger on manually-read (ACTUAL-type) billing imports and explain the 1785 ACTUAL-type disputed bills.

H-FIRMWARE-UNIT-SCALE-MISMATCH.statement: Meter firmware v4.2 (rollout 2026-06) reports raw register values in 0.1 m3 units vs v3.x's m3 units; since BV-17 applies no unit_scaling (E-13), raw v4.2 register values compared against m3-based 12-month history appear ~10x inflated, causing false high-consumption flags on both AMI and manually-read v4.2-firmware meters.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The tariff_change_log returned zero records, indicating no tariff rate changes were made in billing-db during the logged period; this rules out a tariff change as the cause of the wrong bills but says nothing about AMI reads, field read handoffs, staffing, or import validation rules.

The disputed_bills_by_read_type query shows 1240 disputed bills had ESTIMATED reads versus 1785 with ACTUAL reads, meaning the majority of disputes are on bills that used actual (non-estimated) reads rather than estimate substitutions.

re-read under E-12 (accepted premise check) — PR-ROOT: E-12 confirms a specific import-rejection mechanism only for the 1240 ESTIMATED-type disputed bills (all AMI-channel), giving no evidence the rule change also produces incorrect bills on the 1785 ACTUAL-type bills that the root problem relies on as its key differentiator.; PR-CHAIN-3: The confirmed rejection mechanism in E-12 explains only the ESTIMATED-type subset of disputes (reads rejected then substituted as estimates); it provides no evidence the same mechanism produces incorrect bills on ACTUAL-read accounts, which is this premise's explicit claim and the majority of disputes.

crm-tickets.dispute_response_times shows median response time 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets, i.e. response handling is currently within SLA. This does not support treating slow/inadequate response handling as the driver of the dispute surge; it says nothing about bill accuracy causes (AMI reads, field handoffs, staffing, import rules).

E-04.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) states there has been no tariff change this year, a non-authoritative claim that agrees with the already-recorded tool finding E-01 (billing-db tariff_change_log shows zero records). It adds no new decision-relevant information beyond corroborating a question already settled by authoritative tool evidence.

The route-log shows manual-read route completion at 0.88 against a 0.95 target across 9200 manual-read accounts for Aug-Sep 2026, indicating some scheduled manual meter reads were not completed; this is a modest field-execution gap, not a dominant one, since E-02 already shows the majority of disputed bills carry ACTUAL (not estimated) reads.

E-06.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (Field Operations Manager, who has an incentive toward headcount increase) claims field reading staff have been short by three readers since July, causing late routes and resulting estimated bills. This is an unverified stakeholder claim consistent with the mechanism in H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTFALL, but it does not override E-02's authoritative finding that most disputed bills carry ACTUAL (not estimated) reads.

crm-tickets dispute_volume_monthly shows disputes roughly flat at 610/590 in June/July 2026 then jumping to 1180/1260 in August/September 2026, confirming the dispute surge is real, began in August, and roughly doubled — but this says nothing about which upstream cause (AMI reads, field handoffs, staffing, import rules, response handling) is driving it.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 (E-08) is an authoritative document confirming that any route priority change request is executed only after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD), which formalizes the authority basis for the already-recorded K-DISPATCH human-approval constraint on push_route_update; it says nothing about the billing-rule, AMI-read, staffing, or ticket-response causes of the dispute surge.

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db accounts_estimated_last_cycle returns only account_id and route fields for 320 accounts across 40 routes last cycle; it lacks the read_type, tariff, and import_status fields that W-WI-01 intended to use to deepen the disputed-bills-by-read-type analysis, so it does not confirm or extend H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE and gives only a thin, unlinked count of estimate-substitution scale.

E-10.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes returns 14 individual routes (fields: completion, route) with distinct completion values, sample 0.7 for R-00, i.e. some routes fall well below the 0.95 target seen in aggregate (E-05). It confirms the route-completion shortfall is concentrated in a specific, enumerable set of routes rather than uniform, but it carries no account, read-type, or dispute linkage, so it cannot establish how much (if any) of the dispute surge these lagging routes contribute.

E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (non-authoritative, message) claims MDMS export access for Lakeside is now provisioned per vendor ticket TX-4471, which if true would unblock the previously ACCESS_PENDING mdms-export query (read_events_for_disputed_estimated) tied to U-AMI-ACCESS-PENDING / VOB-U-AMI-ACCESS-PENDING. The observation itself contains no AMI read-event data and does not speak to whether AMI reads were actually degraded or valid.

Of 1240 AMI-channel read events tied to disputed ESTIMATED-type bills (matching E-02's ESTIMATED count exactly), 1184 had a valid AMI read delivered before cutoff but were rejected at billing import with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, while only 56 had no AMI read received at all. This shows the dominant driver of ESTIMATED-type disputes is a billing-import rule rejecting high-consumption AMI reads, not AMI read non-delivery.

E-13.content: billing-config.validation_rule_changes → 2 record(s): {"change": "high-consumption check compares raw register value with 12-month m3 history", "deployed": "2026-08-01", "rule": "BV-17", "unit_scaling": "none"}; {"change": "label text", "deployed": "2026-03-02", "rule": "BV-09"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-config.validation_rule_changes confirms rule BV-17 ("high-consumption check compares raw register value with 12-month m3 history", unit_scaling: none) deployed 2026-08-01 — exactly aligned with the August dispute-surge onset (E-07) — matching the REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION mechanism seen in E-12. The second record, BV-09, is an unrelated March 2026 label-text change. The content does not state whether BV-17's check is restricted to AMI-channel reads or also applies to manually-read (ACTUAL-type) billing imports.

mdms-export shows meter firmware v4.2 (rolled out 2026-06, just before the August dispute surge) reports register values in units of "0.1 m3", while firmware v3.x reports in plain "m3". Combined with BV-17's confirmed "unit_scaling: none" raw-register-vs-m3-history comparison (E-13), this is a plausible concrete mechanism for inflated apparent consumption on v4.2-firmware meters, and this mechanism is not inherently limited to the AMI read channel.

problem_definition.requested_solution: SH-CS (Customer Service Director, requester) asked for a single AI agent that auto-answers dispute tickets and autonomously "fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills" (CL-01).
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from 610/590 (Jun/Jul 2026) to 1180/1260 (Aug/Sep 2026) (E-07).
1240 of 3025 disputed bills carry ESTIMATED read type versus 1785 ACTUAL (E-02).
Of AMI read events tied to the 1240 ESTIMATED disputed bills, 1184 had a valid read delivered before cutoff but were rejected at import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-12).
Billing rule BV-17 (raw-register-vs-m3-history, no unit scaling) deployed 2026-08-01, aligned with the surge onset (E-13).
Manual-read route completion is 0.88 against a 0.95 target across 9200 accounts, Aug-Sep 2026 (E-05).
Dispute ticket response times are within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d) (E-03), ruling out slow response handling as a driver.
problem_definition.root_problem: Dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1220/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-07). Billing import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 and comparing raw AMI register values to 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling (E-13), misreads v4.2-firmware meters that report register values in 0.1 m3 units (E-14) as high-consumption, causing billing import to reject an otherwise validly-delivered AMI read (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) and substitute an ESTIMATED bill instead; this accounts for 1184 of the 1240 ESTIMATED-type disputed bills (E-12). This confirmed mechanism explains the ESTIMATED-read share of disputes (41% of 3025, E-02) but does not yet explain the majority of disputes that carry ACTUAL read type (1785 of 3025, E-02), whose cause remains open.

proposal.root_problem: Dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1220/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-07). Billing import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 and comparing raw AMI register values to 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling (E-13), misreads v4.2-firmware meters that report register values in 0.1 m3 units (E-14) as high-consumption, causing billing import to reject an otherwise validly-delivered AMI read (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) and substitute an ESTIMATED bill instead; this accounts for 1184 of the 1240 ESTIMATED-type disputed bills (E-12). This confirmed mechanism explains the ESTIMATED-read share of disputes (41% of 3025, E-02) but does not yet explain the majority of disputes that carry ACTUAL read type (1785 of 3025, E-02), whose cause remains open.

causal_chain: Meter firmware v4.2, rolled out 2026-06, reports raw register values in 0.1 m3 units instead of the m3 units used by prior firmware (E-14).
Billing import validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, compares raw register values directly against 12-month m3-based consumption history with no unit scaling (E-13).
For AMI reads from v4.2-firmware meters, this unit mismatch inflates apparent consumption, triggering a false high-consumption flag at billing import (E-13, E-14).

Billing import rejects the flagged AMI read with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION even though a valid read was delivered before cutoff, for 1184 of 1240 ESTIMATED-type disputed-bill read events (E-12).
The rejected read is substituted with an ESTIMATED-type bill instead of the actual AMI reading (E-12).

Customers receiving these estimated/incorrect bills file dispute tickets, contributing to dispute volume roughly doubling from Jun-Jul to Aug-Sep 2026, coincident with BV-17's August 1 deployment (E-07, E-13).
This confirmed mechanism accounts for the 1240 ESTIMATED-type share of disputed bills but not yet the 1785 ACTUAL-type majority (E-02), whose cause remains open.

proposal.summary: The problem (PD-1@v2, superseding an invalidated earlier framing PD-1@v1) is that dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1220/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-07). A confirmed mechanism was found: billing rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, compares raw meter register values to 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling (E-13); firmware v4.2 (rolled out 2026-06) reports values in 0.1 m3 units versus v3.x's plain m3 units (E-14), so valid AMI reads get falsely flagged high-consumption and rejected, explaining 1184 of the 1240 ESTIMATED-type disputed bills (E-12). A tariff change (E-01) and slow ticket response (E-03) were ruled out. This mechanism explains only ESTIMATED-type disputes; the majority of disputed bills (1785/3025, E-02) are ACTUAL-type, and whether BV-17 also hits manually-read imports is unresolved (open CRITICAL VOB-U-BV17-SCOPE), outside this release's scope. Decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, nothing held, because the critical open question lies outside the released scope (route-completion review plus a conditionally-confirmed route update) and the one in-scope open item (VOB-R-5, staffing contribution) is non-critical. A proposed route-update action was in fact blocked at runtime pending authorization/VOB-R-5. No automated bill writes occurred (per K-BILLWRITE). Known limitations: DEFINE gate only conditional; structural BV-17 fix and re-billing affected accounts are infeasible in available time, leaving wrong bills uncorrected; ACTUAL-type majority unexplained; upstream data-handoff validity unverified; and the original request for an auto-answering agent (CL-01) is not addressed by this design.
